credentials: the github stack's passphrase is the operator passphrase, found through the roots' chain

The passphrase every operator stack is encrypted under, and no CI job
holds, is the operator passphrase: escrow label operator/passphrase,
slot .credentials/operator.passphrase, variable
KLUSTER_OPERATOR_PASSPHRASE, commands `credentials derived
operator-passphrase generate|recover`. The escrowed ciphertext moves
with its label; nothing is re-encrypted.

The operator-stack driver finds it through the account roots'
acquisition chain, now kluster.lib.acquisition: the desktop secret
store, the slot, the variable, then a prompt where stdin is a terminal,
refusing by name where nothing answers. The masters chain and the kit
password read the store through the same module. generate and recover
keep it in the store, and in the slot only on a machine with no store;
the desktop secret store joins rule 6's closed set of channels
(credentials.md §1), as a SecretStore channel in the slot map.

The slot's name is written once, in kluster.lib.stack_environment, and
the credentials package takes it from there.

credentials: the credentials commands find the operator passphrase through the chain

lifecycle.environment no longer recovers the operator passphrase from
the escrow. BackendEnvironment carries the chain as a finder
(stack_environment.operator_passphrase, for the checkout whose slots the
credentials package writes), called only when an operator stack is
asked for, so a command that never points at one never looks. Where the
chain holds nothing the refusal names `credentials derived
operator-passphrase recover`, the escrow being the recovery path.

framework/pulumi.md §3.3, the operator-stack help and docstring,
Pulumi.github.yaml's header, github_secrets and test_mise_env use the
operator passphrase's name and say where it is found.
